newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 27.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- World's largest titanium deposits estimated at 2 billion tons discovered in Hadong-sanchong area in South Kyongsang province.
- National Assembly ratifies Korea's entry into OECD. The ratification document, after President Kim Young-sam signs it, is expected to go to the French government next month.
- About 12,000 Koreans in high-income brackets, mostly in professional occupations, will face tax probe for dishonest filing of income tax returns.
- Korea, Malaysia to hold summit talks in Kuala Lumpur today.
- Korea Telecom develops digital optical cable television system enabling users to view video screens on demand while talking on the telephone.
- Cold spell hits the nation, sending temperatures down to as low as minus 14 degrees C.
- Government, ruling New Korea party near agreement on four-percent hike in rice prices.
- Korean Federation of Employers makes about-face to oppose plural trade unions in the workplace.
- Carl Hunziker, an American detained in North Korea on spy charges, is expected to be released today.
